title: Are You Striking Out With Your DSAR Duties?
summary: See how continuous data discovery helps teams locate personal data, streamline DSAR fulfillment, and reduce manual work and governance gaps.
body_markdown:
### Summary


Data subject access requests (DSARs) can be hard to fulfill when personal data is spread across systems and copies. Continuous discovery helps teams find and understand personal data across the enterprise, reducing manual work and blind spots.


A data subject access request (DSAR) gives an individual the right to ask what personal data an organization holds about them, how that data is used, and who it is shared with. Meeting a DSAR deadline can be difficult when personal data is spread across systems, copied into different environments, or changing over time.


Manual searches can slow fulfillment and make it harder to know whether all relevant data has been found. Continuous discovery helps teams maintain a current view of where personal data lives and how it moves—giving them a stronger foundation to locate responsive data, support timely reviews, and reduce blind spots.


What is a DSAR? A data subject access request (DSAR) gives individuals the right to ask an organization what personal data it holds about them, how it’s used, and who it’s shared with. Regulations like[GDPR](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/information-individuals_en) and[CCPA](https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa) set strict response deadlines, and manual fulfillment drains teams while still leaving governance gaps. The faster and more completely you can find every copy of an individual’s data, the easier DSARs become.


But checking a box on a vendor checklist isn’t the same as knowing you can find every relevant copy of personal data when a DSAR arrives.


## **Yes, you’ve ticked the checkbox. But is it the right checkbox?**


These are the questions victims of ‘Mapping sold as Discovery’ solutions are asking us now.


- Can your solution tell me consistently and sustainably where personal data is that it shouldn’t be – check.
- One of the problems we have had is if we tell the system where the personal data is for ‘discovery,’ how can I trust it to tell me where any personal data is, and it shouldn’t be – check.
- Can your system, consistently and sustainably, create accurate data lineage across all copies and partial copies of the personal data so I can have a high level of confidence? Extra points if it can be done in an automated way to reduce risk – check.
- Can your system consistently and sustainably give me high confidence that if we get a DSAR, it is a real request around data transacted or used by our enterprise? We are having a massive amount of requests; we can’t keep up with the bogus ones – check.
- Can your system, on an ongoing basis, tell me if all personal data is protected – check.
- Can your discovery scale to our size environment as it is not scalable to continuously copy data from our Databases to a mapping solution? We have a huge network – check.
- Can your solution consistently and sustainably ensure the data quality we need to be able to discover all uses of personal data and related data, so we have a high level of quality – check.
